text:
Rae: Quick callout about the first-touch flow: product team mocked a samples carousel (inline) vs a single checklist card with 'Start checklist' CTA. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/first-touch-samples

Omar: Carousel is nice visually but users in tests skimmed images and missed the CTA. Checklist gets straight to action.

Lin: Accessibility note: carousel requires next/prev controls that are keyboard reachable and have clear labels. If we keep carousel, include an 'Open checklist' button in each frame.

Gina: Copy tweak: avoid 'Complete setup' language. Try 'Try these quickstarts' and 'One-click deploy' labels. Also show time estimate: '~2 min' for each sample.

Rae: Nice. What about mobile? Carousel works well on mobile horizontally but checklist is a long scroll. Could show carousel on mobile and checklist as desktop rail.

Omar: Hybrid ok, but telemetry needs variant tag: `first_touch.variant=carousel|checklist|hybrid`. Also track `sample.open` + `sample.deploy.start` events.

Lin: For a11y: announce frame changes via `aria-live="polite"` and ensure pauses for screen reader users. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for auto-advancing carousels (or disable auto-advance).

Gina: UX decision: show a persistent micro-CTA in header 'Continue setup' when checklist incomplete. Gentle reminder, not modal.

DevOpsBot: FYI staging build 0.46.0 includes both variants behind feature flag `first_touch_experiment`.

Rae: I'll update the figma with copy options and mobile/desktop rules, then draft an experiment plan. Any objections to hybrid by default?

Omar: :+1: hybrid makes sense if we measure carefully. Make sure we don't double-count opens (carousel click vs checklist open).
